title: Migrating a plant line from relay logic to a PLC over three weekend shutdowns
summary: Three weekend windows, a hard stop every Sunday at 20:00, and a rollback plan for each phase - the line runs every Monday no matter what.

blocks.eyebrow: A migration plan with no brave Sundays
blocks.title: Relay to PLC in three shutdowns
blocks.body: The line runs five days a week and pays for everything. You get three weekend windows to move it from relay logic to a PLC, and each window ends with the line able to run Monday on either system. That constraint is the plan.

items.label: Weekend shutdowns, each with its own scope
Hard stop, every weekend, no exceptions
Wires landed without a ring-out and a checkmark

blocks.title: The rule that makes this work
blocks.body: You never carry a half-landed change into a production week. If a phase is not proven by Saturday night, you roll back while there is still time - not at 19:40 on Sunday with adrenaline making the decisions.

blocks.heading: The three windows
rows: Panel build and wire landing, outputs only
Every output forces from the PLC with the line in manual
Relays never left the circuit - close the panel and walk away
Inputs and sequence logic, line dry-cycled
Two full dry cycles with no faults
Changeover plug back to relays; troubleshoot on the bench this week
Ten consecutive good cycles at full rate
Plug back to relays; the PLC watches in monitor mode another week
blocks.caption: Each window is independently shippable. That is what makes the deadlines survivable.

items.title: Lockout, tag, verify zero energy
items.detail: The week ends with the line safe, not with wires moved. Nothing else happens Friday.

items.title: Land outputs on the PLC terminal rails
items.detail: One wire, one ring-out, one checkmark. Batch landing is how a crossed pair hides until Saturday night.

items.title: Force every output from the PLC
items.detail: Each solenoid, contactor, and lamp proven individually with the line in manual.

items.title: Punch-list whatever did not force
items.detail: A missed output becomes a weekday bench job, not a Sunday scramble.

items.title: Hard stop
items.detail: Panel closed, line back on relays for Monday. Weekend 1 is done either way.

blocks.heading: The changeover plug is the rollback
items: Build the wiring so either the relay panel or the PLC can drive the outputs through one keyed plug.
The plug makes rollback a single motion, not a rewiring session.
No wire leaves the relay panel until the PLC has run production for a full week.
Only after that week do you strip the old logic - and you still keep the prints.

blocks.heading: Two brains, one line, three weeks

nodes.title: Field devices
nodes.detail: Sensors and pushbuttons stay common to both systems.

nodes.title: Changeover plug
nodes.detail: Keyed plug selects which brain drives the outputs.

nodes.title: Relay panel
nodes.detail: The proven system. Untouched until the PLC earns retirement.

nodes.title: PLC
nodes.detail: The new system. Proven in stages: outputs, then logic, then rate.

blocks.heading: What migrates and what never does
blocks.body: Safety circuits - e-stops, gate switches, the safety relay - stay hardwired and outside the PLC program from start to finish. The migration covers sequence logic only: timers, counters, interlocks of convenience. If removing power from the PLC must not disable a function, that function was never the PLC's to hold.

items.label: Every input forced and seen in the PLC's input table
items.detail: Including the ones you are sure about.

items.label: Two full dry cycles with zero faults
items.detail: One good cycle proves it ran once. Two starts to prove it runs.

items.label: E-stop drop tested from both gate positions
items.detail: Safety is hardwired, but you prove the wiring after a panel rebuild.

items.label: Punch list written down, not remembered
items.detail: Monday-you deserves a list, not a vibe.

blocks.title: Rollback is not failure
blocks.body: If Sunday noon arrives with an unexplained fault, the plan says roll back and find it on the bench during the week. The hard deadline is what keeps a brave Sunday night from becoming a ruined Monday.

blocks.heading: The paperwork nobody wants
blocks.body: An updated I/O list, wire numbers as actually landed, and red-lined prints after each weekend. The next person to open this panel - possibly you, at 02:00 in a year - inherits whatever you wrote down. The PLC program gets printed and taped inside the door with the date on it.

blocks.heading: Check the plan
blocks.prompt: It is 19:30 on Sunday of Weekend 2. The dry cycle shows one intermittent fault you have not explained. What does the plan say to do?
options: Run one more test and decide at 19:55
Roll back to relays and troubleshoot on the bench during the week
Leave the PLC in charge but watch it closely on Monday
blocks.explanation: The hard stop exists so the decision is made by the plan, not by adrenaline. An intermittent fault plus a production Monday is exactly the combination the rollback was built for.
